newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cook says UK should join EMU if it success - paper.
newsitem.headline: Cook says UK should join EMU if it success - paper.

text.p: Britain should join the planned European single currency if it proves successful, Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said in a newspaper interview on Wednesday.

"If monetary union is launched and it's a success, I have already said that in the long term Britain should join," said Cook, who has a reputation for being a sceptic on monetary union but pro-European on many other issues.
The single currency is due to start on January 1, 1999.
Asked whether Britain could sign up for monetary union in 2002, he told the afternoon daily Le Monde it would not be "appropriate at this stage to fix a specific date".
He pledged, however, Britain would "do everything" in its power to facilitate the euro's introduction when it takes over the presidency of the European Union in the first half of 1998.
Cook, who has been busy staking out a new Euro-friendly policy since Labour's landslide win in Britain's May 1 election, said he wanted the country to have a "fresh start" in Europe.
The Conservatives' "policy of isolation brought us nothing".
He said Britain was unlikely to take part in the first wave of monetary union as there was only 18 months to go before the 1999 launch date and the government had a heavy agenda.
"If we decided at this belated stage that monetary union should be a priority, it would have a big impact on the other things we want to do," he said.
British Prime Minister Tony Blair had said it was "unlikely we could join the first wave, and if we do not join in the first wave, it is unlikely we could join the year after", he added.
Labour has said any decision to scrap sterling would have to be endorsed by a referendum.
One attraction of monetary union was that it would eliminate speculation among European currencies which would "give a lot of security to our exporters", Cook said.
But in an echo of France's call for a political counterweight to the future European central bank, he said the European finance ministers' council would have to be strengthened under monetary union.

"If we're going to have a single currency with a central bank which decides monetary policy, it will be necessary to reinforce the Ecofin council to ensure this monetary policy goes hand-in-hand with an economic strategy for jobs, growth, and production", he said.

While saying it is fully committed to the independence of the European central bank, France has called for a stability council to be set up to coordinate economic, fiscal and currency policy inside the euro zone.
Cook said that Britain recognised its place was in Europe and wanted to be an "equal partner" with Germany and France but would not abandon its sovereignty.
"Foreign policy touches the heart of national identity", he said. Countries need not hold identical views on everything.
"Germany and France often have different positions. France sometimes puts forward its own national interest which does not prevent it from playing its role in reaching solutions.
"Britain should follow a similar approach," he said.
-- Penny MacRae, Paris Newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
